title: Fix fake/hardcoded metrics and unsafe error handling in App.tsx
description: App.tsx is the actual live entry component (index.html -> src/main.tsx -> App.tsx) and contains several concrete, verifiable bugs: (1) Line 278: const movementIntensity = Math.random() * 0.5 + 0.2; // Mock movement detection -- the Movement Intensity metric shown live in the UI (pose-metrics grid) and included in exported JSON is pure random noise, not derived from actual pose motion, despite README advertising Motion Tracking with velocity/acceleration analysis. (2) Line 287: poseDuration: (timestamp - (timestamp - 1000)) / 1000, // Mock duration -- this expression is a compile-time constant: (timestamp - (timestamp - 1000)) always equals 1000, so poseDuration always equals exactly 1, never reflecting real elapsed pose time. (3) Line 503 inside handleExport: duration: Date.now() - (Date.now() - 60000) -- same pattern, always evaluates to exactly 60000ms; every exported session file reports a fixed 60-second session duration regardless of actual session length. (4) Line 408: catch (err) { ... setError() } accesses .message on an untyped/unknown catch variable with no instanceof Error guard, unlike the correct pattern already used two blocks earlier in the same file at line 185 (const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : ...). Given tsconfig.json has strict: true (which enables useUnknownInCatchVariables), this is a real type-safety gap, not just style. Acceptance criteria: movementIntensity is computed from actual frame-to-frame keypoint position deltas (pose history is already available via poseMetrics/currentPose state each frame -- track previous keypoints in a ref and compute a real magnitude-of-change metric) rather than Math.random(). poseDuration and the export session duration are computed from a real tracked start timestamp (e.g. a ref set when tracking/session begins) rather than the constant-collapsing expressions. The catch block at line ~406-408 uses the same instanceof Error guard pattern as line 185. Existing tests still pass; if no test currently covers processFrame or handleExport, add a minimal vitest test asserting movementIntensity is not derived from Math.random and that duration reflects elapsed time, not a hardcoded constant.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: Precise text for item 4 (lost shell-quoting on original description): line 406-408 reads: catch (err) { console.error(FrameProcessingError, err); setError(TemplateLiteral with err.message here) } -- err.message is accessed on the unknown catch variable with no instanceof Error narrowing, unlike line 185 in the same file.

title: PWA claim is non-functional: served index.html has no manifest/service-worker; dead duplicate public/index.html references nonexistent sw.js
description: README.md headlines PWA Ready: Installable as a Progressive Web App as a shipped feature. Verified false as of 2026-07-30 for the actual build output. Two index.html files exist: root index.html (the real Vite entry -- referenced by <script type=module src=./src/main.tsx>, and confirmed to be what actually ships: dist/index.html, the real build output, has ZERO occurrences of manifest or serviceWorker via grep) and public/index.html (a separate, unused duplicate that DOES contain <link rel=manifest href=/manifest.json> and a navigator.serviceWorker.register(/sw.js) call). Vite treats files under public/ as static passthrough assets copied into dist/, so public/index.html is never used as the HTML entry point -- it is dead weight that happens to look like the real thing, which is likely why the PWA wiring silently regressed (someone edited the unused copy, not the real one). Compounding this: /sw.js, the service worker file public/index.htmls own dead script tries to register, does not exist anywhere in the repo (find . -iname sw.js -not -path ./node_modules/* returns nothing) -- so even restoring the registration call would 404. public/manifest.json itself is valid and present, just not linked from the real entry. Separately (same audit pass, unrelated root cause, bundling per this repos existing convention of grouping small dead-artifact findings into one bead as bf-46h does): webpack.config.js at repo root is not referenced by any npm script (package.json scripts are dev/build/preview via vite, lint via eslint, test via vitest, test:e2e via cypress -- grep -n webpack package.json matches nothing) and is not covered by bf-46hs enumerated dead-code list. Acceptance criteria: (1) either add <link rel=manifest href=/manifest.json> to the real root index.html and implement or restore a working service worker at public/sw.js so navigator.serviceWorker.register(/sw.js) actually succeeds, making the README PWA claim true, OR remove the PWA claim from README.md plus delete the dead public/index.html duplicate and its non-functional SW registration script -- pick one, do not leave the current half-wired state; (2) delete public/index.html if choice is the removal path, or merge its manifest/SW-registration lines into the real root index.html if choice is the fix path -- do not leave two index.html files in the repo; (3) delete unused webpack.config.js (confirm zero references first via grep across package.json and any CI/build scripts); (4) npm run build succeeds and dist/index.html reflects whichever choice was made.

title: Remove dead/orphaned code: stale .backup files, broken src/index.tsx, duplicate SettingsPanel, unconditional debug components
description:
Concrete dead/orphaned code found via grep + diff audit (none of it is reachable from the real app entry index.html -> src/main.tsx -> App.tsx):

(1) src/services/PoseDetectionService.ts.backup (103 lines) is a stale, much older version of the current src/services/PoseDetectionService.ts (632 lines) -- diff shows substantially different content (missing motion tracking fields, different constructor). No .ts.backup extension is ever imported by TypeScript/Vite, so this is inert clutter.

(2) src/services/PoseSmoothingService.ts.backup is a byte-for-byte identical duplicate of src/services/PoseSmoothingService.ts (diff produces zero output) -- pure redundant file.

(3) src/index.tsx imports MainApplication from './components/MainApplication', but no such file exists anywhere in the repo (find src -iname 'MainApplication*' returns nothing). This file is not referenced by index.html (which loads src/main.tsx, not src/index.tsx), not in vite.config.ts, and not in package.json. It is a broken, unreachable entry point left over from an earlier/parallel build attempt.

(4) Two duplicate, unused SettingsPanel components exist: src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx and src/components/Settings/SettingsPanel.tsx. Neither is imported by App.tsx or any other file (grep -rn "SettingsPanel" src/ --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts across the whole tree only matches each file's own definition).

(5) App.tsx unconditionally renders two components explicitly commented as temporary: '{/* Diagnostic Component - Temporary for debugging */} <PoseDetectionDiagnostic />' and '{/* Simple Pose Test - Temporary for debugging */} <SimplePoseTest />'. There is zero import.meta.env.DEV or similar dev-only gating anywhere in src/ (grep -rn "import.meta.env" src/ returns nothing), so these debug-only components ship unconditionally to production users at gait.jedarden.com.

Acceptance criteria:
- Delete both .ts.backup files (confirm via grep that nothing imports the .backup path first).
- Either restore/wire up a real MainApplication component or delete the orphaned src/index.tsx; if src/index.ts (no 'x', the barrel-export file) is confirmed genuinely unused too (not referenced by package.json main/module/exports and not imported by tests), remove it as well, otherwise leave it and note why it's kept.
- Remove both unused SettingsPanel.tsx files, or wire exactly one of them into the app if settings functionality is desired (do not keep two dead duplicates either way).
- Gate PoseDetectionDiagnostic and SimplePoseTest behind an import.meta.env.DEV check (or remove them from App.tsx entirely) so they no longer render in production builds.
- npm run build and existing test suite still pass after cleanup.

title: Route App.tsx console.log/console.error calls through existing LoggingService.ts (per-frame logging at 60fps)
description: docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 Decision item 4 calls for routing App.tsx debug console.log calls through a level-gated logger so they no-op by default in production, matching the README claim Performance Optimized: Runs at 60+ FPS. Verified as of 2026-07-30: src/services/LoggingService.ts exists in the repo but is not imported or used anywhere (grep -rn LoggingService src --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts only matches its own definition file). Meanwhile src/App.tsx contains 29 raw console.log/console.error calls (grep -n "console\.\(log\|warn\|error\)" src/App.tsx), several of which run inside processFrame -- the function invoked on every requestAnimationFrame tick, i.e. up to ~60 times/sec while the camera is running -- for example line 224 console.log(processFrame called - video:...), line 253-254 (frame number and video dimensions logged every frame), and line 260 console.log(Detected poses:, poses.length, poses) which serializes the full pose/keypoint array to the console on every frame. This is a real production perf/noise cost (console serialization of arrays at 60Hz blocks the main thread measurably in Chrome devtools) not just style. This gap is distinct from bf-2k6 (fixes fabricated metric values, does not touch logging) and bf-46h (dead-code removal and DEV-gating two diagnostic components, does not touch App.tsx logging calls). Acceptance criteria: App.tsx per-frame debug logs (inside processFrame) are routed through LoggingService.ts (or removed if genuinely just leftover debug output) so they are no-ops in production builds by default; startup/lifecycle logs (service init, camera init, start/stop/reset handlers) may remain but should also go through LoggingService for consistency; verify via npm run build + manual smoke that no console spam occurs per-frame in a production build; existing tests continue to pass.

description: Evidence: cypress/e2e/gait-detection-app.cy.ts references 55 distinct data-testid selectors (gait-detection-app, app-title, camera-selector, start-camera-button, stop-camera-button, gait-confidence, stride-length-value, cadence-value, calibration-dialog, export-dialog, person-1-gait-params, mobile-layout, sr-announcements, etc — grep -oh "data-testid=\"[^\"]*\"" cypress/e2e/gait-detection-app.cy.ts | sort -u). Only 6 data-testid attributes exist anywhere in src/ (start-button, stop-button, reset-button, export-button, confirm-export, error-message — in ControlPanel.tsx and ExportDialog.tsx), and even the overlapping ones use different id strings than cypress expects (cypress wants start-camera-button/stop-camera-button, src has start-button/stop-button; cypress wants confirm-export-button, src has confirm-export). App.tsx itself (the actual entry rendered via index.html -> src/main.tsx -> App.tsx) has zero data-testid attributes. The cypress spec appears written against an aspirational multi-person gait-analysis UI (calibration dialog, per-person gait parameters, responsive breakpoints, accessibility announcements) that was never wired into the shipped App.tsx — none of GaitAnalysisPanel.tsx, GaitDetectionSystem.ts, or the Settings/Calibration UI are imported by App.tsx or main.tsx. Net effect: npm run test:e2e currently cannot pass a meaningful fraction of its assertions against the real app. Acceptance criteria: (1) Run npm run test:e2e (or npx cypress run) against the actual dev server and record which specs/assertions fail due to missing selectors. (2) Add data-testid attributes to App.tsx and/or its rendered children (CameraSelector, ControlPanel, error banner, video/canvas container) for every UI element that IS actually implemented today, matching the naming cypress already expects where reasonable (e.g. start-camera-button, camera-status, video-container, error-message, pose-confidence) rather than renaming cypress ids arbitrarily. (3) For assertions/describe blocks that reference features not implemented in the current App (multi-person tracking, gait calibration dialog, stride/cadence/symmetry gait parameters, mobile/tablet/desktop responsive layout testids, sr-announcements) either remove them or mark them .skip with a comment pointing at the missing feature — do not fabricate fake DOM just to satisfy the assertion. (4) npm run test:e2e passes cleanly (no failures) after the change, and any skipped specs are clearly annotated with why. Keep scope to test-id reconciliation + removing/skipping dead assertions; do NOT attempt to build the full aspirational multi-person/calibration UI in this bead.

title: Wire GaitAnalysisService/ApplicationCoordinator/VideoDisplay/PoseOverlay/SkeletonRenderer into App.tsx (ADR-001 component swap-in)
description: docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) documents that src/App.tsx -- the actual entry point rendered at gait.jedarden.com via src/main.tsx -- hand-rolls its own getUserMedia call, requestAnimationFrame loop, and canvas drawing, and imports NONE of the substantial existing architecture: src/services/ApplicationCoordinator.ts, src/services/GaitAnalysisService.ts (real cadence/stride-length/symmetry-index/gait-phase computation from keypoint history, exercised by tests/unit/services/GaitAnalysisService.test.ts, tests/GaitAnalysisService.test.ts, tests/integration/GaitDetectionPipeline.test.ts, tests/integration/ApplicationIntegration.test.ts), src/components/VideoDisplay.tsx, src/components/PoseOverlay.tsx, src/components/SkeletonRenderer.ts. Verified still true as of 2026-07-30: grep -n import src/App.tsx src/main.tsx shows App.tsx imports only ControlPanel, PoseDetectionService, PerformanceMonitor, PoseDetectionDiagnostic, SimplePoseTest, CameraSelector -- zero references to ApplicationCoordinator/GaitAnalysisService/VideoDisplay/PoseOverlay/SkeletonRenderer anywhere in App.tsx or main.tsx. The ADR splits its Decision into shippable beads: (1) remove fabricated metrics -- filed and in progress as bf-2k6, (2) component swap-in -- this bead, NOT yet filed anywhere in the 24-bead workspace history, (3) gate debug-only components behind DEV -- covered by bf-46h, (4) route per-frame console.log through LoggingService -- filed separately as a plan-gap bead. This bead covers ADR-001 Decision item 1 only: replace the hand-rolled getUserMedia/draw loop in App.tsx with ApplicationCoordinator + VideoDisplay + PoseOverlay/SkeletonRenderer, and wire GaitAnalysisService into the frame loop so the UI shows real computed GaitParameters (cadence, stride length, symmetry index, gait phase) instead of nothing -- gait.jedarden.com currently ships keypoint-dot pose detection only, not the gait analysis the product is named for and the README headlines (Gait Analysis: Specialized algorithms for walking pattern detection). Acceptance criteria: App.tsx (or a thin wrapper around ApplicationCoordinator) renders VideoDisplay + PoseOverlay/SkeletonRenderer instead of the inline canvas-drawing code in processFrame; GaitAnalysisService is instantiated and fed keypoint history each frame; at least one real GaitParameters field (cadence, stride length, symmetry index, or gait phase) is displayed in the live UI and included in the export payload from handleExport; existing GaitAnalysisService/ApplicationCoordinator tests continue to pass; npm run build succeeds. This is a scoped incremental rewrite of App.tsx internals only -- the external URL, container, and deployment pipeline are unaffected per the ADR. Given the scope, this bead may warrant mitosis-splitting by whoever claims it rather than being done as one large change (per the ADR own guidance).

title: Audit Cypress test coverage and feature implementation
description: Catalog all data-testid selectors expected by cypress/e2e/gait-detection-app.cy.ts (grep -oh 'data-testid="[^"]*"' | sort -u) and compare against what actually exists in src/ (grep -rh 'data-testid' src/). Produce a three-column classification: (1) Expected by cypress, (2) Actually exists in src/ (with file location), (3) Status: IMPLEMENTED / PARTIAL / NOT_IMPLEMENTED. For IMPLEMENTED features, note any id mismatches (e.g. cypress expects 'start-camera-button', src has 'start-button'). For PARTIAL, note what's missing. For NOT_IMPLEMENTED, list the missing feature (e.g. calibration dialog, multi-person gait params, sr-announcements). Save the classification to .beads/cypress-audit.md. Acceptance: (1) .beads/cypress-audit.md exists with complete classification table, (2) Each of the 55 cypress data-testids is categorized, (3) Clear list of IMPLEMENTED features that need id additions/fixes, (4) Clear list of NOT_IMPLEMENTED features to skip in cypress.
